SOURCE INFORMATION

Date: 2026-10-21 11:26 UTC
Source: StarFox 64. MoonFox uses original geometry, characters, mission and sound; no source-game assets.
Tech: my-3D2dge agent edition 0.59.1; Three.js 0.180.0; JavaScript, WebGL2, HTML/CSS and Web Audio. Build: esbuild 0.25.12. Tests: Playwright 1.56.1.
Environment: Codex CLI; Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS / WSL2; Chrome 154.0.8037.57.
Model: OpenAI; requested gpt-6-astra / high; runner codex. Exact serving model: unknown.

ART & ANIMATION

Art direction: Sunlit ocean science fiction; angular spacecraft, monumental coastal ruins, a teal-and-cream palette, cyan lasers and coral enemy fire. All geometry is procedural and original.

Animation: Procedural transforms, smooth steering and banking, barrel rolls, homing projectiles, particles and shader ocean waves; my-3D2dge runs the fixed-step 120 Hz simulation.

ENGINE FEEDBACK · 1

Liked most: The compact manual, deterministic fixed-step clock, mapped keyboard/gamepad actions, procedural music and saved settings.

Stuck or guessed wrong: I initially assumed audio-unlock and rumble helpers existed in the agent edition. Browser tests exposed those assumptions; sound now uses the documented music/SFX entry points, and vibration uses the standard Gamepad API when available.

Most important custom system: The perspective flight-combat system and reusable mission event director, including wingmate rescue, routes, checkpoints and carrier phases.

ENGINE FEEDBACK · 2

Hardest part: Connecting a perspective renderer and swept 3D hit tests to the engine’s primarily fixed-camera 2D rendering conventions.

Remove or overhaul: The split between full-edition and agent-edition documentation; available methods should be unambiguous in each generated API card.

One change: Add a documented perspective-renderer adapter with matching projection and collision examples.

PROMPT FEEDBACK · 404299fcd4

Liked most: Controller-first UX, a kiosk attract mode and a single-file release made the desired product concrete.

Confusing: “Feature-complete” and “all infrastructure” have no finite content boundary. This build treats them as a finished replayable mission, reusable prefabs and editable mission-event source.

Hardest thing: Balancing approachable flight controls, mission pacing and the complete encounter loop in one polished slice.

One additional test: A living-room playtest using a physical DualSense controller at television viewing distance.

TESTING

Seven integration-suite runs (initially 30 checks, expanded to 35; final result 35/35), three smoke runs, one visual/realtime run, and one targeted browser diagnostic. The full AI mission reached all four stages, defeated the carrier and looped. Realtime attract entry was observed at 11.002 seconds in software-rendered headless Chrome, on the first rendered frame after the ten-second threshold. Twelve issues were fixed: eleven game/integration issues and one test-harness issue; one was critical and prevented startup. Final browser runtime errors: zero. Physical DualSense hardware and test execution cost: unknown.
